parameters.formDescription: Runs the CEC spec-kit delivery flow for a Rally story with Claude Code on the host, runs the repo's Terraform plan against a non-prod environment from the feature branch, then opens a DRAFT pull request linking that plan. If Claude needs to ask you something about the nonprod plan it posts to Slack and waits. Takes 30–120 minutes; follow progress under Executions.

leave empty for the repo's default branch

parameters.jsCode:
const c = $input.first().json;
return [{ json: { kind: 'script', name: 'rally-story', label: 'Fetch Rally Story', args: [c.storyId], timeoutMin: 2 } }];

const c = $('Build Context').first().json;
const phase = `PHASE 1/6 — seed + specify.
${c.workspace.constitutionMissing ? `0. This repo has no spec-kit constitution yet. First run the speckit-constitution skill (with the
   cec-sdlc:cec-constitution overlay) to write .specify/memory/constitution.md from what this
   repository actually is: its language, frameworks, test setup and conventions.
` : ''}1. Run the cec-sdlc:cec-rally-seed skill for ${c.storyId}. It fetches the Story and its parent
   Feature and assembles the seed. If the Rally MCP tools are unavailable, use the story snapshot
   below as the seed instead. If the seed shows the story is NOT scoped to ${c.repo}, stop and
   report BLOCKED.
2. Run the speckit-specify skill with that seed as the feature description. Leave genuine open
   questions as [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers; the next phase resolves them.
3. Reply with the feature directory path (specs/...) and a 3-line summary.

Story snapshot, fetched from the Rally REST API when the pipeline started:
---
${c.storyText}
---`;
return [{ json: {
  kind: 'claude',
  label: "Seed + Specify",
  model: c.models.dev,
  retryModel: c.models.retry,
  cwd: c.runDir,
  timeoutMin: 45,
  requireStatusOk: true,
  prompt: `${c.preamble}\n\n${phase}\n${c.statusRule}`,
} }];

const c = $('Build Context').first().json;
const phase = `PHASE 2/6 — clarify.
Run the speckit-clarify skill on the current feature spec (the newest directory under specs/).
You are the only one who can answer its questions. Answer each one yourself, picking the option
best supported by the Rally story, the existing code and conventions in this repo, and
cec-knowledge. Apply the answers to spec.md exactly as the skill normally would.

Then add (or extend) a section at the end of spec.md:

## Assumptions (autonomous clarify)
| # | Question | Chosen answer | Why |

List every question you answered, including any [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers you resolved.
Reviewers will check this table on the PR, so be specific. No [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers may
remain in spec.md when you finish.`;
return [{ json: {
  kind: 'claude',
  label: "Clarify",
  model: c.models.dev,
  retryModel: c.models.retry,
  cwd: c.runDir,
  timeoutMin: 30,
  requireStatusOk: true,
  prompt: `${c.preamble}\n\n${phase}\n${c.statusRule}`,
} }];

const c = $('Build Context').first().json;
const phase = `PHASE 6/6 — implement.
Run the speckit-implement skill for the current feature, working through tasks.md in order and
checking each task off as you finish it.
- Run the repository's build and tests with its own tooling (see plan.md) and fix any failure you
  introduced. If they cannot run in this environment (missing services, credentials, etc.), say
  exactly what you could not run and why.
- FIRST commit the spec-kit artifacts for traceability — specs/ (spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md and
  the rest), plus .specify/ and .claude/skills/ if this pipeline added them — with message
  "${c.storyId}: spec-kit artifacts". Do this before the code so the specs are on the branch even
  if implementation stalls. Then commit the implementation in logical steps, every message
  prefixed "${c.storyId}: ".
- Do not push.
Reply with: tasks done, tasks skipped (and why), and the test commands you ran with their results.`;
return [{ json: {
  kind: 'claude',
  label: "Implement",
  model: c.models.dev,
  retryModel: c.models.retry,
  cwd: c.runDir,
  timeoutMin: 150,
  requireStatusOk: true,
  prompt: `${c.preamble}\n\n${phase}\n${c.statusRule}`,
} }];

const c = $('Build Context').first().json;
const phase = `FINAL STEP — write the pull request description. Do not change any files.
Read the current feature's spec.md (including "Assumptions (autonomous clarify)"), plan.md and
tasks.md, and run: git log --oneline origin/${c.workspace.base}..HEAD and git diff --stat origin/${c.workspace.base}...HEAD

Output ONLY the PR body as GitHub-flavoured markdown: no preamble, no closing remarks, no code
fence around the whole body, and no STATUS line. Use these sections:
## Summary
## Rally
${c.story.url} (${c.storyId}: ${c.story.name})
## What changed
## Autonomous clarify assumptions
(copy the assumptions table verbatim; reviewers must check these)
## Tasks
(done / skipped, with the reason for anything skipped)
## Tests
(what ran and the results; what could not run)
## Open questions & risks

Do not write a nonprod / Terraform plan section: the pipeline appends one with the run link.`;
return [{ json: {
  kind: 'claude',
  label: "Write PR Body",
  model: c.models.discovery,
  retryModel: c.models.retry,
  cwd: c.runDir,
  timeoutMin: 15,
  requireStatusOk: false,
  prompt: `${c.preamble}\n\n${phase}`,
} }];

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ text: $json.slackText, blocks: [ { type: 'section', text: { type: 'mrkdwn', text: $json.slackText } } ] }) }}

parameters.jsCode:
const c = $('Build Context').first().json;
// qa = every question the developer has answered over Slack so far; Collect Answers and
// Read Decision carry it back here for the next round.
const qa = $input.first().json.qa ?? [];
const answered = qa.length
  ? `\n\nThe developer already answered these over Slack. Their answers are authoritative:\n` +
    qa.map((x, i) => `Q${i + 1}: ${x.question}\nA${i + 1}: ${x.answer}`).join('\n\n')
  : '';
const phase = `NONPROD PLAN — find the target. Do not change any files.
Before the pull request is opened, the pipeline runs this repository's own GitHub Actions
Terraform plan against a NON-PRODUCTION environment, from branch ${c.workspace.branch}. Work out
which workflow and inputs do that. The pipeline runs it with nonprod-plan.sh; you only decide.

1. Read .github/workflows/*.yml and find what runs \`terraform plan\`: directly, through a reusable
   workflow (\`uses:\`; read org ones with gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/contents/<path>), a composite
   action or a Makefile target.
2. Work out how it is triggered: workflow_dispatch (inputs, types, options, defaults, required) or
   push to branches that ${c.workspace.branch} matches. workflow_dispatch only works when the
   workflow file also exists on the repository's default branch.
3. Work out the right non-production environment from \`environment:\` keys, env / tfvars / backend
   directories (envs/, environments/, *.tfvars), gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments, the
   inputs of past successful nonprod runs (gh run list --workflow <file> --json ..., then
   gh run view <id>), and cec-sdlc:cec-knowledge for this workload's environments and accounts.
   Prefer the environment the team itself uses for pre-merge plans.
4. The inputs must run PLAN ONLY. Never choose apply or destroy. If the workflow cannot plan
   without also applying, ask.
5. Unlike the other phases, this one CAN ask the developer, but only through the "questions"
   array below; they answer over Slack and this phase runs again with their answers. Ask when it
   matters instead of guessing: more than one plausible non-prod environment, a required input
   you cannot ground, or no Terraform plan workflow at all. Give options and your recommendation.
Never run gh workflow run, gh run rerun, or gh api with a write method.${answered}

End your reply with a \`\`\`json fenced block in exactly this shape, then the STATUS line:
{
  "workflow": "<file name in .github/workflows, e.g. terraform-plan.yml>",
  "trigger": "workflow_dispatch or push",
  "environment": "<non-prod environment name>",
  "inputs": { "<input name>": "<string value>" },
  "planOnly": true,
  "skip": false,
  "rationale": "<why this workflow, environment and inputs>",
  "evidence": ["<file:line or run URL>"],
  "questions": [ { "question": "...", "options": ["..."], "recommendation": "..." } ]
}
"inputs" is {} for push. "questions" is [] when you are confident; when it is not empty, fill
the other fields with your best current guess. Set "skip": true only if the developer
explicitly answered that this story needs no nonprod plan.`;
return [{ json: {
  kind: 'claude',
  label: 'Discover Nonprod Plan',
  model: c.models.dev,
  retryModel: c.models.retry,
  cwd: c.runDir,
  timeoutMin: 30,
  requireStatusOk: true,
  prompt: `${c.preamble}\n\n${phase}\n${c.statusRule}`,
  qa,
} }];
